newsitem.title: USA: Wyser-Pratte/Providence say COMSAT suit meritless.
newsitem.headline: Wyser-Pratte/Providence say COMSAT suit meritless.

text.p: Wyser-Pratte Inc and Providence Capital Inc said Friday that the suit filed against them by COMSAT Corp is without merit and that they intend vigorously to defend themselves if the suit is not withdrawn.
In a joint statement, Herbert Denton, president of Providence, and Guy Wyser-Pratte, president of Wyser-Pratte, said, "There is no question that COMSAT's complaint against us is without merit...."
Further, they said, "If management does not withdraw this action promptly, we intend to vigorously defend ourselves."

COMSAT announced on Thursday it had filed a suit against its former chief executive, Bruce Crockett, alleging a conspiracy linking him with Herbert Denton, and the shareholder group of Providence Capital and Wyser-Pratte which proposed a proxy contest with COMSAT .
COMSAT's suit charges the privately held firms violated the Communications Satellite Act of 1962.

The defendants' activities also allegedly violate a 1996 Termination Agreement in which Crockett agreed with COMSAT not to disparage, compete with or disclose confidential information about COMSAT to third parties.

In their joint response to the suit, Denton and Wyser-Pratte said that "after being forced to reschedule the annual meeting under pressure from shareholders, (COMSAT) management has now resorted to intimidating shareholders...."

The shareholder group had asked for a special shareholders meeting after COMSAT postponed its annual meeting in March, originally scheduled for May 16. The request was later withdrawn after COMSAT announced earlier this month it would hold an annual meeting on August 15.
